title: Post-Course Portfolio: Food Delivery Backend
descriptionMarkdown:
# Food Delivery Backend

## Position in the curriculum
Post-course portfolio expansion: build after finishing the full curriculum through the final capstone, ideally after the E-commerce Backend, whose checkout/inventory and idempotency patterns this project extends into a longer, multi-actor order lifecycle (customer, restaurant, courier) instead of a single buyer-seller transaction.

## Already-proven foundation
The E-commerce Backend already required a transactional checkout and an explicit order-status state machine. This project extends that state machine across three different actors, each of whom is only permitted to trigger specific transitions — a richer authorization-plus-state-machine problem than any earlier catalog entry.

## Project scope
Model `Restaurant` (with a menu of `MenuItem`s, each with availability), `Order` (a customer, a restaurant, line items, a status), and `Courier`. The order state machine: `PLACED` (by the customer) -> `ACCEPTED`/`REJECTED` (by the restaurant only) -> `PREPARING` -> `READY_FOR_PICKUP` -> `PICKED_UP` (by an assigned courier only) -> `DELIVERED` (by the assigned courier only) -> or `CANCELLED` (by the customer, only while still `PLACED`). Enforce, per transition, that only the correct actor role may trigger it, and that an invalid transition (skipping a state, or a customer attempting to mark their own order `DELIVERED`) is rejected with a clear error, never silently accepted. Reject an order for a menu item that has since become unavailable, checked at order time inside the same transaction that creates the order. Add a simple courier-assignment step (assign the nearest available courier from a small fixed list; a real distance calculation is optional) once an order reaches `READY_FOR_PICKUP`.

## Required evidence
- A full state-machine test suite covering every valid transition and at least five specific invalid ones (wrong actor, wrong current state, or both).
- A test confirming an order for a now-unavailable menu item is rejected inside the same transaction that would have created it, with no partial order row left behind.
- An authorization test confirming a courier cannot see or act on an order not assigned to them.
- A concurrency test where two orders are placed for the last available unit of a limited-quantity menu item, confirming only one succeeds.
- A written diagram of the full state machine, with each transition labeled by the actor permitted to trigger it.

## Review and completion
A reviewer walks an order through its full lifecycle as three different authenticated identities in sequence (customer places, restaurant accepts, courier picks up and delivers), then creates a second order and attempts an invalid transition as the wrong actor at each state, expecting a specific, correctly-attributed rejection every time rather than a generic error.
learningObjectives: Model a multi-actor state machine where each transition is restricted to a specific role
Validate a business precondition (item availability) inside the same transaction that depends on it
Prevent a limited-quantity race across concurrent orders with a database-enforced guarantee
Design and test authorization scoped to a specific assignment (this courier's assigned orders only)
Document a state machine's transitions and their permitted actors as a reviewable artifact
